artists.biography:
Simple Minds are a Scottish rock band who achieved worldwide popularity from the mid-1980s to the early 1990s. 
The band produced a number of critically acclaimed albums in the early 1980s and best known for their No. 1 US, Canada and Netherlands hit single "Don't You (Forget About Me)", from the soundtrack of the John Hughes film The Breakfast Club. They are also known for the No. 3 US hit single "Alive and Kicking" and the No. 1 UK hit single "Belfast Child". The band has sold more than 60 million albums since 1979. 
The core of the band is the two remaining founder members - Jim Kerr (vocals, songwriting) and Charlie Burchill (guitars, keyboards after 1990, other instruments, songwriting) - and drummer Mel Gaynor (who first joined the band in 1982). The other current band members are Andy Gillespie (keyboards) and Ged Grimes (bass guitar). Significant former members include bass guitarist Derek Forbes and keyboard player Michael MacNeil (the latter credited as a significant band composer during the band's rise in the 1980s).

perplexity.description:
Once Upon a Time, released on 21 October 1985 through Virgin Records, is the seventh studio album by Scottish band Simple Minds. Marking a pivotal moment in their career, the album blends electronic, rock, and pop elements into a polished, stadium-ready sound that defined mid-1980s rock. Produced by Jimmy Iovine and Bob Clearmountain, it features anthemic tracks with expansive arrangements and synthesizer textures, showcasing the band's evolution from their earlier post-punk and art-rock roots into mainstream international stars.

Commercially, Once Upon a Time became Simple Minds' most successful album, reaching number 1 in the UK and the Netherlands, and breaking into the top 10 in the US and several other countries. It spawned four hit singles—"Alive and Kicking," "All the Things She Said," "Sanctify Yourself," and "Ghost Dancing"—all of which charted well internationally. The album's success was bolstered by the band's recent breakthrough in the US with "Don't You (Forget About Me)," although that track was notably excluded from the original album release. The record sold over two million copies within two months, cementing Simple Minds' status as global rock icons and defining the sound of mid-80s arena rock.

Critically, Once Upon a Time is regarded as a landmark album that balanced commercial appeal with artistic ambition. The production by Iovine and Clearmountain contributed to its polished, radio-friendly sound, while the band's songwriting—primarily by Jim Kerr, Charlie Burchill, and Mick MacNeil—delivered memorable melodies and evocative lyrics. The album's visual presentation, including artwork by Anton Corbijn, complemented its sonic identity, making it a classic example of 1980s rock craftsmanship and a key entry in Simple Minds' discography.
